summary: This section sets out the statutory definitions of when an employee is treated as dismissed by their employer. It provides that dismissal occurs where the employer terminates the contract, where a limited-term contract expires without renewal, or where the employee resigns in response to the employer's conduct. It also treats an employee as dismissed if the employee serves counter-notice to leave on an earlier date during the employer's notice period.

elements.requirement: The employer terminates the employee's contract of employment, with or without notice.
elements.quote: the contract under which he is employed is terminated by the employer (whether with or without notice)

elements.requirement: A limited-term contract ends due to the occurrence of the limiting event and is not renewed under the same contract.
elements.quote: he is employed under a limited-term contract and that contract terminates by virtue of the limiting event without being renewed under the same contract

elements.requirement: The employee terminates the employment contract, with or without notice, in circumstances where the employer's conduct entitles them to terminate without notice.
elements.quote: the employee terminates the contract under which he is employed (with or without notice) in circumstances in which he is entitled to terminate it without notice by reason of the employer’s conduct

elements.requirement: The employer gives notice to terminate the contract of employment.
elements.quote: the employer gives notice to the employee to terminate his contract of employment

elements.requirement: During the employer's notice period, the employee gives notice to end the contract on a date earlier than the expiry of the employer's notice.
elements.quote: at a time within the period of that notice the employee gives notice to the employer to terminate the contract of employment on a date earlier than the date on which the employer’s notice is due to expire
